title: The Factory Return Is Free
prompt_md:
## Goal
Show that returning a freshly built object from a factory function costs zero copies in C++17, while copying from a named variable does cost one.

## The feature (lesson 14.15)
Write a copy constructor for `Coord` that prints a line whenever it runs, so copies are observable. The provided `make` returns a prvalue (`return Coord{v};`), which C++17 guarantees is elided — no copy. In `main`, `Coord a = make(v);` therefore prints nothing, but `Coord b = a;` copies from a named lvalue and runs your copy constructor.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: one integer per line

## Output
For each value, exactly two lines: `copy <value>` (printed by the one real copy, `b = a`) followed by `value <value>`. The factory return produces no copy line.

test_cases.label: Hidden: four values
test_cases.expected_stdout:
copy 10
value 10
copy 20
value 20
copy 30
value 30
copy 40
value 40

title: Prvalue Argument vs Lvalue Argument
prompt_md:
## Goal
Demonstrate that passing a temporary (prvalue) by value is elided in C++17, while passing a named variable by value is copied.

## The feature (lesson 14.15)
Write the copy constructor for `Coord` so it prints a line when it runs. The provided `inspect` takes its parameter by value. Calling `inspect(Coord{v})` passes a prvalue, which C++17 constructs directly into the parameter — no copy. Calling `inspect(local)` passes a named lvalue, which is copied.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: one integer per line

## Output
For each value, in order: `inspect <value>` (from the prvalue call, no copy), then `copy <value>` (the copy of the named variable), then `inspect <value>` again (from the lvalue call).

test_cases.label: Sample: two values
test_cases.expected_stdout:
inspect 4
copy 4
inspect 4
inspect 1
copy 1
inspect 1

test_cases.label: Hidden: three values
test_cases.expected_stdout:
inspect 0
copy 0
inspect 0
inspect 7
copy 7
inspect 7
inspect 55
copy 55
inspect 55
